questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal aortic arch (left) with a congenital abnormality of the arch (right). In this defect, where is the narrowing most commonly located?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the bifurcation of the aorta into the common iliac arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the aortic root within the sinuses of Valsalva

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the abdominal aorta at the level of the renal arteries

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the descending aorta, just distal to the left subclavian artery

explanation.summary: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).
explanation.whyCorrect: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).

questions.stem: This clinical photograph shows bluish discoloration of the nailbeds, fingers, and toes in an infant. This physical sign is a direct marker of what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated carboxyhemoglobin from carbon monoxide exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: An elevated concentration of deoxygenated hemoglobin in the blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: An absolute deficiency of total hemoglobin (anemia)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased methemoglobin from an oxidizing drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess bilirubin deposition in the skin and mucous membranes

explanation.summary: Cyanosis is the bluish discoloration seen when the level of deoxygenated hemoglobin rises (roughly above 5 g/dL). In right-to-left shunting cyanotic CHDs, poorly oxygenated blood reaches the systemic circulation, producing peripheral and central cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis is the bluish discoloration seen when the level of deoxygenated hemoglobin rises (roughly above 5 g/dL). In right-to-left shunting cyanotic CHDs, poorly oxygenated blood reaches the systemic circulation, producing peripheral and central cyanosis.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a young child assuming a squatting/knee-to-chest posture during a hypercyanotic 'tet' spell. Why does this position relieve the child's symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It raises systemic vascular resistance, which decreases right-to-left shunting across the VSD

choices.label: B
choices.text: It slows the heart rate, allowing longer diastolic filling of the left ventricle

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lowers systemic vascular resistance, increasing forward flow through the aorta

choices.label: D
choices.text: It increases pulmonary vascular resistance, forcing blood into the systemic circuit

choices.label: E
choices.text: It compresses the inferior vena cava, reducing venous return to the right heart

explanation.summary: Squatting kinks the femoral arteries and increases systemic (arterial) vascular resistance. This raises left-sided pressures, reducing the right-to-left shunt across the VSD so that more deoxygenated blood is directed through the pulmonary valve to be oxygenated, easing the tet spell.
explanation.whyCorrect: Squatting kinks the femoral arteries and increases systemic (arterial) vascular resistance. This raises left-sided pressures, reducing the right-to-left shunt across the VSD so that more deoxygenated blood is directed through the pulmonary valve to be oxygenated, easing the tet spell.
